NASA Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) funds early-stage interstellar propulsion studies, including fusion and beamed-energy concepts. Together these programs form the telescope arrays foundation that Exoplanet Survey Swarms will build on — the survey propulsion results, the target ranking methods, and the institutional memory.

title: Exoplanet Survey Swarms Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Exoplanet Survey Swarms: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Exoplanet Survey Swarms — telescope swarms cataloging worlds before ships arrive.

Phase 1 — Prove (telescope arrays): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (survey propulsion): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (target ranking): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (atmospheric analysis): survey hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and exoplanets-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
